newsitem.title: USA: Supreme says Ind. plant problems continue.
newsitem.headline: Supreme says Ind. plant problems continue.

text.p: Supreme Industries Inc, a maker of truck bodies and shuttle buses, said it continues to have start-up problems with a fiberglass-reinforced panel plant in Ligonier, Ind.
"The facility has not produced commercially acceptable product," Supreme said.
The company said it has determined that certain machine components were damaged in early experimental operation and will need to be replaced.

"The receipt of the customized replacement components and rectifying the problem may take six to twelve months. Management is of the opinion that with these modifications the FRP facility will produce commercial-quality FRP panels," the company said.
Supreme on Monday reported revenues for the first quarter of 1997 increased $44.2 million from $38.5 million for the corresponding quarter last year.
Net income for the quarter advanced to $1.7 million, or $0.18 per share, a 70.9 percent improvement over $986,000, or $0.11 per share, for last year's first quarter.
